_readme: Catalog for the Explorer dashboard. Earth satellites are tracked live from CelesTrak orbital elements (NORAD catalog number) and propagated with SGP4 in the browser. Orbit sizes for Moon and Mars orbiters come from the missions' published orbits; heliocentric probes use published distances and speeds. 'match' checks that CelesTrak returned the object we expect.

earth.name: International Space Station
earth.purpose: Orbiting laboratory where astronauts live and test how to survive long missions — exactly what this game is about.
facts: Circles Earth about every 92 minutes, so the crew sees about 16 sunrises a day.
Recycles about 98% of the crew's water, including sweat and urine.

earth.name: Tiangong (China Space Station)
facts: Has been crewed continuously since 2022.

earth.name: Hubble Space Telescope
earth.purpose: Space telescope that observes in visible, ultraviolet and near-infrared light.
facts: Was serviced by Space Shuttle astronauts five times.
Has made more than 1.6 million observations.

earth.name: Terra
earth.purpose: Earth-observing flagship: clouds, fires, land, oceans and air quality.
facts: Its MODIS camera sees the whole Earth every 1–2 days.

earth.name: Aqua
earth.purpose: Studies Earth's water cycle: rain, sea ice, clouds and water vapour.
facts: Crosses the equator in the early afternoon every day.

earth.name: Landsat 9
earth.purpose: Maps Earth's land surface: forests, farms, cities and glaciers.
facts: Landsat satellites have imaged Earth continuously since 1972.

earth.name: Landsat 8
earth.purpose: Works with Landsat 9 so every place on Earth is imaged every 8 days.
facts: Each pixel covers 30 × 30 m of ground.

earth.name: NOAA-20 (JPSS-1)
earth.purpose: Polar weather satellite: its data feeds daily weather forecasts.
facts: Passes over each pole 14 times a day.

earth.name: ICESat-2
earth.purpose: Laser altimeter measuring ice sheet height and sea ice thickness.
facts: Fires its laser 10,000 times a second.

earth.name: GPM Core Observatory
earth.purpose: Measures rain and snow around the world with a space radar.
facts: Leads a fleet of satellites that maps global rainfall every 30 minutes.

earth.name: SWOT
earth.purpose: Surveys the height of oceans, rivers and lakes.
facts: Measures more than 90% of Earth's surface water.

earth.name: Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich
earth.purpose: Measures sea level rise to within a few centimetres.
facts: Continues a sea-level record that started in 1992.

earth.name: PACE
earth.purpose: Studies plankton, aerosols and clouds in more than 200 colours.
facts: Its hyperspectral camera can tell different kinds of plankton apart.

earth.name: GOES-18 (GOES West)
earth.purpose: Geostationary weather satellite watching the Americas and the Pacific.
facts: Geostationary: it circles Earth once a day, so it hovers over one spot.
Also carries a space-weather monitor that watches solar flares.

earth.name: GOES-19 (GOES East)
earth.purpose: Geostationary weather satellite watching the Americas and the Atlantic.
facts: Carries CCOR-1, a coronagraph that spots solar storms heading for Earth.

earth.name: TESS
earth.purpose: Planet hunter: finds exoplanets passing in front of nearby stars.
facts: Its unusual 13.7-day orbit is in resonance with the Moon, which keeps it stable.

orbiters.name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter
orbiters.purpose: Maps the whole Moon in high detail and measures its temperature and radiation.
facts: Photographed the Apollo landing sites, including the astronauts' footpaths.
Found the coldest measured places in the Solar System inside polar craters (about −250 °C).

orbiters.name: Chandrayaan-2 orbiter
orbiters.purpose: Studies the Moon's surface minerals, water ice and thin atmosphere.
facts: Its radar looks for ice hidden in permanently shadowed craters.

orbiters.name: Danuri (KPLO)
orbiters.purpose: Korea's first Moon mission. Carries NASA's ShadowCam to see inside dark polar craters.
facts: ShadowCam is 200 times more sensitive than LRO's camera, so it can image craters lit only by reflected light.

orbiters.name: CAPSTONE
orbiters.purpose: Microwave-oven-sized CubeSat testing the 'halo' orbit planned for Artemis's Gateway station.
facts: Its orbit swings close over the north pole and far over the south pole, keeping the south pole in view of Earth.

orbiters.name: ARTEMIS P1 (THEMIS-B)
orbiters.purpose: Studies how the solar wind flows around the Moon.
facts: Started as a THEMIS Earth satellite and was sent to the Moon in 2011.

sites.name: Shackleton crater · your base
sites.purpose: The south pole region where this game's Moon base sits. Crater rims nearby get sunlight most of the year.
facts: The crater floor never sees the Sun and may hold water ice.
NASA's Artemis landing regions are all near the south pole.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 (Vikram & Pragyan)
sites.purpose: First landing close to the lunar south pole.
facts: Pragyan rover confirmed sulphur in the south polar soil.

sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus
sites.purpose: First US landing on the Moon since 1972 and the first commercial one.
facts: Caught a leg on landing and tipped onto its side, but still sent back data.

sites.name: IM-2 Athena
sites.purpose: Landed near Mons Mouton, the closest any spacecraft has landed to the south pole.
facts: Carried NASA's PRIME-1 ice drill.

sites.name: Chang'e-4 & Yutu-2
sites.purpose: First soft landing on the far side of the Moon.
facts: Its radiation detector measured 1.37 mSv per day — the Moon number used in this game.

sites.name: Chang'e-6
sites.purpose: Brought back the first samples ever collected on the far side.
facts: Returned 1,935 g of far-side soil to Earth in June 2024.

sites.name: Blue Ghost Mission 1
sites.purpose: First fully successful commercial Moon landing, in Mare Crisium.
facts: Filmed a sunset from the Moon's surface.

sites.name: Apollo 11 · Tranquility Base
sites.purpose: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin took humanity's first steps on another world.
facts: With no wind or rain, the bootprints should last for millions of years.
A laser reflector left here is still used to measure the Earth–Moon distance.

sites.name: Apollo 17 · Taurus-Littrow
sites.purpose: The last time people walked on the Moon (so far).
facts: Geologist Harrison Schmitt found orange volcanic glass here.

sites.name: North pole · Peary crater
sites.purpose: Nothing has landed near the Moon's north pole yet. Parts of Peary crater's rim are lit by the Sun most of the time.
facts: Nearby Hermite crater is among the coldest places measured in the Solar System (LRO Diviner).

orbiters.name: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
orbiters.purpose: Its HiRISE camera can see objects the size of a kitchen table. Relays rover data to Earth.
facts: Photographed Perseverance's parachute coming down on landing day.

orbiters.name: 2001 Mars Odyssey
orbiters.status: Operating (oldest active Mars spacecraft, low on fuel)
orbiters.purpose: Found water ice just below the surface and relays rover data.
facts: Its radiation instrument measured what astronauts would get in Mars orbit.

orbiters.name: MAVEN
orbiters.purpose: Studied how Mars lost most of its atmosphere to the solar wind.
facts: Showed that solar storms strip gas from Mars's upper atmosphere faster.

orbiters.name: Mars Express
orbiters.purpose: Europe's first Mars mission: 3D maps and radar studies under the polar caps.
facts: Its radar found signs of liquid water under the south polar ice.

orbiters.name: ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter
orbiters.purpose: Sniffs Mars's air for methane and other trace gases.
facts: Also relays data from NASA's rovers.

orbiters.name: Emirates Mars Mission (Hope)
orbiters.purpose: Mars's first weather satellite: watches the whole planet's weather through the day.
facts: Its high orbit lets it see the full disc of Mars.

orbiters.name: Tianwen-1 orbiter
orbiters.purpose: Delivered the Zhurong rover and maps Mars from orbit.
facts: China's first independent mission to another planet.

orbiters.name: Phobos (moon)
orbiters.purpose: The bigger of Mars's two small moons. It goes round Mars three times a day.
facts: Slowly spiralling inward: in about 50 million years it will break up or crash into Mars.

orbiters.name: Deimos (moon)
orbiters.purpose: The smaller, outer moon of Mars.
facts: From the surface of Mars it looks like a bright star.

sites.name: Perseverance · Jezero crater
sites.purpose: Searches for signs of ancient life in a dried-up river delta and collects rock samples for return to Earth.
facts: Jezero was a lake about 3.5 billion years ago.
Its MOXIE experiment made oxygen out of Mars's CO₂ air.

sites.name: Ingenuity helicopter · Jezero
sites.purpose: First powered, controlled flight on another planet (19 April 2021).
facts: Flew 72 times — planned for just 5.
Now works as a weather station and its last photos show a broken blade.

sites.name: Curiosity · Gale crater
sites.purpose: Found that Gale crater once held lakes that could have supported microbes.
facts: Its RAD detector measured 0.67 mSv per day on the surface — the Mars number in this game.

sites.name: Zhurong rover · Utopia Planitia
facts: Went into hibernation for the Martian winter and dust stopped it waking up.

sites.name: InSight · Elysium Planitia
sites.purpose: Listened for marsquakes and measured Mars's core.
facts: Detected more than 1,300 marsquakes.

sites.name: Phoenix · north polar plains
sites.purpose: Landed in Mars's arctic and touched water ice just under the soil.
facts: Saw snow falling from clouds (it melted away before reaching the ground).

sites.name: North polar ice cap (Planum Boreum)
sites.purpose: A dome of water ice about 1,000 km across and up to 3 km thick.
facts: In winter a layer of frozen CO₂ (dry ice) settles on top, then turns back into gas in spring.

sites.name: Viking 1 · Chryse Planitia
sites.purpose: First US spacecraft to land on Mars and send pictures from the surface.
facts: Worked for more than six years.

helio.name: James Webb Space Telescope
helio.purpose: The biggest space telescope: sees the first galaxies in infrared light.
facts: Orbits the Sun–Earth L2 point, 1.5 million km from Earth, always on Earth's night side.
Its sunshield is the size of a tennis court.

helio.name: SOHO
helio.purpose: Watches the Sun non-stop from the L1 point, 1.5 million km sunward of Earth.
facts: Amateurs using its images have discovered more than 5,000 comets.

helio.name: Parker Solar Probe
helio.purpose: Flies through the Sun's outer atmosphere, the corona.
facts: Closest approach 6.1 million km from the Sun's surface (24 Dec 2024).
Fastest object ever built: about 690,000 km/h at closest approach.

helio.name: Voyager 1
helio.purpose: The farthest human-made object. Crossed into interstellar space in 2012.
facts: Around November 2026 it becomes one light-day away from Earth.
Carries the Golden Record of sounds and pictures from Earth.

helio.name: Voyager 2
helio.purpose: The only spacecraft to have visited Uranus and Neptune.
facts: Entered interstellar space in November 2018.

helio.name: New Horizons
helio.purpose: First visit to Pluto (2015) and to the Kuiper Belt object Arrokoth (2019).
facts: Radio signals take more than 8 hours to reach it.

helio.name: Juno
helio.purpose: Studies Jupiter's interior, magnetic field and its moons.
facts: Solar-powered even at Jupiter, with three 9-metre solar wings.
